transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
The White House is rolling out a new program
just two weeks before the crucial midterm elections
that will determine control of Congress.
President Trump says it's a $25 million program
to reward "tifsters" who report alleged fraud
to the federal government.
If you turn somebody in and you, let's say, report
and you find a billion dollars,
we are giving a commission to that person of 1%.
It's in response to mounting voter concerns
about perceived government corruption.
The Justice Department will run the program
and award up to $30,000 to anyone who submits a tip
that results in a successful fraud conviction.
Beef could play a decisive role in this year's midterms.
Ground beef cost $6.80 a pound,
nearly a dollar more adjusted for inflation
than it did when President Trump took office.
But beef producers are also feeling the pain
and it could sway tight races and even red states.
And here's Daniel Kurtzleben has more.
President Trump in August expanded the quota
for lean beef trimmings that could come into the country
under lower tariffs.
It was a move intended to lower ground beef prices,
but it made life tougher for beef producers.
Scott Berger raises cattle in eastern Iowa.
That surprise with a very volatile market already
with a tight supply hurts us really, really fast
and really, really hard.
Trump's beef import policy has become an important topic
in Iowa's closed Senate race,
and political strategists say it could also affect
the state's house and gubernatorial races.
Several more major beef-producing states
are also midterm battlegrounds,
including Nebraska, Texas, and Kansas.
Danielle Kurtzleben, NPR News.
Ukraine's President Philoetomir Zelensky says
Kyiv's early warning systems have resumed
after talking with Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
But Rubio says the U.S. never did anything
deliberately to hurt Ukraine.
And Zelensky met with U.S. negotiator Steve Whitcoff
in Oslo today.
Florida is preparing for the state's 18th execution
of the year.
William Reeves is set to die by lethal injection tonight.
Reagan McCarthy from member station WFSU has more.
Reeves, who is 77, is convicted of shooting
and killing Deputy Richard Rakowski in 1986
after the two struggled over a gun.
While lethal injection has faced increased scrutiny
following the failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee,
Florida has continued what some call an aggressive use
of the death penalty.
Another Florida prisoner was put to death last week.
Unlike in Tennessee, Florida uses a three-drug protocol
for lethal injection.
On Monday, more than 100 veterans sent a letter
to Florida Governor Ron DeSantis urging him to stop the execution,
noting that Reeves was diagnosed with post-traumatic
stress disorder related to his service in Vietnam.
For NPR News, I'm Regan McCarthy in Tallahassee.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Police in Australia have charged a man with intentionally
causing serious injury to an Australian member of Parliament
after 65-year-old Helen Haynes was hit by a car outside her office yesterday
in what authorities say was a targeted attack.
She's hospitalized in critical condition.
Police say the suspect has a court date tomorrow.
This says lawmakers around the world face increased security concerns.
Ending routine vaccinations against hepatitis B for all newborns
could result in far more people reaching adulthood
with chronic infections.
And here's Maria Godoy has more.
The hepatitis B virus attacks the liver.
There's no cure.
And chronic infection can lead to serious outcomes
like liver cancer and death.
The risks are much higher for people infected as infants.
Last December, advisors chosen by Health Secretary
Robert F. Kennedy Jr. recommended that instead of vaccinating
all newborns against Hep B, parents should decide on vaccination
at no earlier than two months of age.
The new study found that delaying vaccination by two months
could lead to a 19% increase in people with chronic infections by age 20.
Shifting to shared decision-making between parents and doctors
could result in an 83% jump.
The findings appear in the Annals of Internal Medicine.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
The Japanese spacecraft is on its way to the larger of Mars's two moons,
Phobos, in hopes of bringing back soil samples to Earth,
which would be a first.
Despite successfully landing nine spacecraft on Mars
and China scoring a touchdown, no one's ever reached either of Mars's moons.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: President Trump launches $25 million program rewarding tips on federal fraud, two weeks before midterms
Trump's lean beef import policy squeezes cattle producers and becomes a midterm issue in Iowa
Zelensky says Kyiv's early warning systems resumed after talks with Secretary of State Marco Rubio
Florida prepares to execute William Reeves, 77, its 18th execution this year, by lethal injection
Australian man charged after MP Helen Haynes was hit by a car outside her office
Ending universal newborn hepatitis B vaccination could significantly raise chronic infection rates, study finds
Japanese spacecraft heads to Mars's moon Phobos to attempt first-ever soil sample return to Earth
